bullets.point: A February 2025 BAFA update to the EnEfG guidance introduced a '90%-Regelung': an EnMS or UMS must now cover at least 90% of an obligated company's total final energy consumption, and BAFA states this rule applies strictly to the single obligated enterprise and NOT across a corporate group. A site-by-site threshold flag does not capture this coverage logic — a the company site above 7.* GWh may already sit inside a certified company EnMS, and the reviewer should weigh whether pure per-site exceedance meaningfully predicts residual obligation.

European Commission guidance on the underlying EU Directive interprets the threshold test as an enterprise-level assessment in which all linked enterprises within EU territory are aggregated, while only entities located in a Member State are obliged. This confirms the pipeline's own grain-mismatch limitation but sharpens it: the legally correct §8 test would aggregate the company's linked entities, something a DE-only, per-site screen with an unresolved company identifier structurally cannot reproduce.

The statutory §8 EnMS establishment deadline has already lapsed: companies that had reached the >7.* GWh three-year-average status by 17 November 2023 were required to have an EnMS or UMS in place by 18 July 2025, with later-qualifying companies given 20 months from their trigger date.
